problems.problem: Compute $\left((1-i)(i-1)\right)^4$.
Show that the function $f:(-3,3)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\ln\dfrac{3-x}{3+x}$ is odd.
Determine the integer solutions of the inequality $x^2+2x-8<0$.
How many elements of the set $A=\{1,2,3,\ldots,100\}$ are divisible by $4$ or by $5$?
In the coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $M(1,-2)$, $N(-3,-1)$ and $P(-1,2)$. Determine the coordinates of the point $Q$ such that $MNPQ$ is a parallelogram.
Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=6$, $AC=3$ and $BC=5$. Compute the length of the altitude $[AD]$.

Consider the system $$\begin{cases} x-2y-8z=-65\\ 3x+y-3z=22\\ x+y+z=28\end{cases}$$ where $x,y,z\in\mathbb{R}$, and the matrix of the system $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2&-8\\3&1&-3\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$.

(a) Show that the rank of the matrix $A$ is equal to $2$.

(b) Solve the system in $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$.

(c) Determine the number of solutions of the system in the set $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$.

Consider the set of matrices $A=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix}\;\middle|\; a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_5\right\}$.

(a) Determine the number of elements of the set $A$.

(b) Show that there exists a nonzero matrix $M\in A$ such that $\begin{pmatrix}\hat{3}&\hat{1}\\-\hat{1}&\hat{3}\end{pmatrix}\cdot M=\begin{pmatrix}\hat{0}&\hat{0}\\\hat{0}&\hat{0}\end{pmatrix}$.

(c) Solve the equation $X^2=I_2$ in the set $A$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\operatorname{arctg}\dfrac{x}{x+1}$.

(a) Determine the equation of the asymptote to the graph of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.

(b) Study the monotonicity of the function $f$.

(c) Determine the inflection points of the function $f$.

Let $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the sequence $I_n=\displaystyle\int_n^{n+1}\frac{2x-1}{x}\,dx$.

(a) Show that the sequence $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$ is strictly increasing.

(b) Show that the sequence $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$ is bounded.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty} n(2-I_n)$.
Which of the numbers $2\sqrt[3]{6}$ and $3\sqrt[3]{3}$ is larger?
Determine the range (set of values) of the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=|x|$.
Determine $m\in\mathbb{R}$ for which the equation $x^2-x+m^2=0$ has two equal real solutions.
Determine the number of rational terms in the expansion of $\left(1+\sqrt[4]{2}\right)^{41}$.
In the coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(2,1)$, $B(-2,3)$, $C(1,-3)$ and $D(4,a)$, where $a\in\mathbb{R}$. Determine $a\in\mathbb{R}$ such that the lines $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel.
Let $A=\left\{0;\dfrac{\pi}{6};\dfrac{\pi}{2};\pi;\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right\}$. What is the probability that an element chosen from the set $A$ is a solution of the equation $\sin^3x+\cos^3x=1$?

Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\\a&0&0\end{pmatrix}\in M_3(\mathbb{R})$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}^*$ we denote $B_n=A^n+A^{n+1}+A^{n+2}$.

(a) Show that $A^{2010}=a^{670}\cdot I_3$.

(b) Determine $a\in\mathbb{R}$ for which $\det(B_1)=0$.

(c) Determine $a\in\mathbb{R}$ for which all the matrices $B_n$, $n\in\mathbb{N}^*$, are invertible.

On the set $\mathbb{R}$ the law $x*y=2xy-3x-3y+m$, $m\in\mathbb{R}$, is defined. Let $M=\mathbb{R}\setminus\left\{\dfrac{3}{2}\right\}$.

(a) Determine $m\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $x*y\in M$ for all $x,y\in M$.

(b) For $m=6$, show that $(M,*)$ is a group.

(c) For $m=6$, prove that the function $f:M\to\mathbb{R}^*$, $f(x)=2x-3$ is an isomorphism between the groups $(M,*)$ and $(\mathbb{R}^*,\cdot)$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{2x-1}-\sqrt[3]{2x+1}$.

(a) Write the equation of the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of the graph with abscissa $x=0$.

(b) Determine the equation of the horizontal asymptote to the graph of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty}\left(\dfrac{f(1)+f(2)+\ldots+f(n)}{-\sqrt[3]{2n+1}}\right)^{\sqrt[3]{2n}}$.

Consider the sequence $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$, $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1\frac{x^n\,dx}{x^2+x+1}$.

(a) Compute $I_1+I_2+I_3$.

(b) Show that the sequence $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$ is decreasing.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty} I_n$.
Show that $\left(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{5}\right)\cap\mathbb{Z}=\{2\}$.
Determine the real values of $m$ for which the line $x=2$ is the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=x^2+mx+4$.
Solve the equation $\sin\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$ in the set $[0,2\pi)$.
Determine $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $n\ge2$, for which $C_n^2+A_n^2=18$.
Determine $a\in\mathbb{R}$ for which the lines $d_1: ax+y+2011=0$ and $d_2: x-2y=0$ are parallel.
Let $x$ be a real number satisfying the equality $\operatorname{tg}x+\operatorname{ctg}x=2$. Show that $\sin2x=1$.

Consider the matrix $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&x&x^2\\0&1&2x\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, where $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Show that $A(x)\cdot A(y)=A(x+y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Show that $\left(A(x)-A(y)\right)^{2011}=O_3$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

(c) Determine the inverse of the matrix $A(x)$, where $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

Consider $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$ and the polynomial $f=X^3+(1-\alpha)X^2+(\alpha-2)iX+\alpha+(\alpha-2)i\in\mathbb{C}[X]$.

(a) Show that the polynomial $f$ has the root $-1$.

(b) Show that if $p,q$ are complex numbers and the polynomial $g=X^2+pX+q\in\mathbb{C}[X]$ has two distinct complex conjugate roots, then $p$ and $q$ are real numbers and $p^2<4q$.

(c) Determine $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$ for which the polynomial $f$ has two distinct complex conjugate roots.

Consider the function $f:(1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\ln(x+1)-\ln(x-1)$.

(a) Show that the function $f$ is strictly decreasing on $(1,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the asymptotes of the graph of the function $f$.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to+\infty} xf(x)$.

Consider the function $f:[1,2]\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-3x+2$.

(a) Compute $\displaystyle\int_1^4 f\left(\sqrt{x}\right)dx$.

(b) Compute the area of the region bounded by the graph of the function $g:[1;2]\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{x}$ and the axis $Ox$.

(c) Show that $(4n+2)\displaystyle\int_1^2 f^n(x)\,dx+n\int_1^2 f^{n-1}(x)\,dx=0$.
Compute the common ratio of the geometric progression $(b_n)_{n\ge1}$ with positive terms, if $b_1+b_2=6$ and $b_3+b_4=24$.
Determine $a\in\mathbb{R}$ for which the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=(1-a^2)x+4$ is constant.
Solve the inequality $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^x<\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^x$ in the set of real numbers.
Determine the number of rational terms of the expansion $\left(1+\sqrt{2}\right)^{10}$.
Compute the distance from the point $A(2,2)$ to the line determined by the points $B(1,0)$ and $C(0,1)$.
Triangle $ABC$ has the angle $A$ of measure $60^\circ$, $AB=4$ and $AC=5$. Compute $\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}$.

Consider the set $H=\left\{A\in M_2(\mathbb{R})\;\middle|\; A^2=A\right\}$.

(a) Show that $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\in H$.

(b) Prove that if $A\in H$, then $A^n\in H$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.

(c) Show that the set $H$ is infinite.

Consider the polynomial $f=(X+i)^{10}+(X-i)^{10}$, with algebraic form $f=a_{10}X^{10}+a_9X^9+\ldots+a_1X+a_0$, where $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{10}\in\mathbb{C}$.

(a) Determine the remainder of the division of the polynomial $f$ by $X-i$.

(b) Show that all the coefficients of the polynomial $f$ are real numbers.

(c) Prove that all the roots of the polynomial $f$ are real numbers.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^5-5x+4$.

(a) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to2}\dfrac{f(x)-f(2)}{x-2}$.

(b) Show that the graph of the function $f$ has an inflection point.

(c) Show that for every $m\in(0,8)$ the equation $f(x)=m$ has exactly three distinct real solutions.

Consider the function $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=e^{-x}$.

(a) Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^1 g(x)\,dx$.

(b) Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^5g(x^3)\,dx$.

(c) Prove that the sequence $(I_n)_{n\ge1}$ defined by $I_n=\displaystyle\int_1^n g(x^3)\,dx$ is convergent.
Compute the modulus of the complex number $(1+i)^2$.
Determine the coordinates of the intersection points of the graphs of the functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+2x$ and $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=-x-2$.
Solve the inequality $2^{x+1}\le4$ in the set of real numbers.
Compute the probability that, choosing at random one of the three-element subsets of the set $A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, the elements of the chosen subset are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression.
Consider the vectors $\vec{u}=\vec{i}-2\vec{j}$ and $\vec{v}=a\vec{i}-\vec{j}$. Determine the real number $a$ for which $\vec{u}\cdot\vec{v}=3$.
Compute the cosine of the angle $A$ of the triangle $ABC$ in which $AB=4$, $AC=5$ and $BC=7$.

Consider the system $$\begin{cases}2x+y+3z=0\\ x+2y+3z=0\\ x+y+mz=0\end{cases}$$ where $m\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Compute the determinant of the matrix of the system.

(b) Determine the real values of $m$ for which the system has a unique solution.

(c) In the case $m=2$, determine the solution $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ of the system for which $x_0>0$ and $x_0^2+y_0^2+z_0^2=3$.

Consider the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-2\\3&-2\end{pmatrix}\in M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and the set $G=\left\{X(p)=I_2+pA\;\middle|\; p\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1\}\right\}$.

(a) Show that $X(p)\cdot X(q)\in G$ for all $X(p),X(q)\in G$.

(b) Assume that $(G,\cdot)$ is a commutative group with identity element $X(0)$. Determine the inverse of the element $X(p)$ in this group.

(c) Solve the equation $\left(X(p)\right)^3=I_2+7A$, where $X(p)\in G$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^3-12x$.

(a) Show that the function is increasing on the interval $[2,+\infty)$.

(b) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to+\infty}\dfrac{e^x}{f(x)}$.

(c) Determine the set of real numbers $a$ for which the equation $f(x)=a$ has three distinct real solutions.

Consider the function $f:(-1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+3}{x+2}$.

(a) Show that every antiderivative of $f$ is strictly increasing on $(-1,+\infty)$.

(b) Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^1\frac{f(x)}{x+1}\,dx$.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to+\infty}\dfrac{\int_x^{2x}f(t)\,dt}{x}$.
Determine the real number $m$ knowing that the sets $A=\{2\}$ and $B=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}\mid x^2+mx+4=0\right\}$ are equal.
Determine the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola associated with the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-3x+2$.
Solve the inequality $3^{\log_3x}<1$ in the set of real numbers.
Compute the probability that, choosing at random one of the two-digit natural numbers, it consists only of odd digits.
Determine the real number $a$ for which the vectors $\vec{u}=3\vec{i}+a\vec{j}$ and $\vec{v}=a\vec{i}+(2a-3)\vec{j}$ are collinear.
Compute the radius of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, knowing that $AB=AC=5$ and $BC=6$.

In $M_3(\mathbb{C})$ consider the matrices $I_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos x&0&i\sin x\\0&1&0\\i\sin x&0&\cos x\end{pmatrix}$, where $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Compute $\det\left(A(\pi)\right)$.

(b) Show that $A(x)\cdot A(y)=A(x+y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $x$ for which $\left(A(x)\right)^{2012}=I_3$.

On the set $G=(0,1)$ the associative law of composition $x\circ y=\dfrac{xy}{2xy-x-y+1}$ is defined.

(a) Show that $e=\dfrac{1}{2}$ is the identity element of the law of composition “$\circ$”.

(b) Show that every element of the set $G$ is invertible (has a symmetric element) with respect to the law of composition “$\circ$”.

(c) Prove that $f:G\to\mathbb{R}_+^*$, $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x}-1$ is an isomorphism from the group $(G,\circ)$ to the group $(\mathbb{R}_+^*,\cdot)$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{e^x+e^{-x}}{2}$.

(a) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to+\infty}\dfrac{x}{f(x)}$.

(b) Prove that the function $f$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

(c) Show that the function $g:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=f\left(\sqrt{x}\right)$ is strictly increasing on $(0,+\infty)$.

For every nonzero natural number $n$ consider the numbers $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^n\cdot\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx$ and $J_n=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin^nx\,dx$.

(a) Compute $J_1$.

(b) Compute $I_1$.

(c) Prove that $J_{2n}-J_{2n+2}=I_{2n}$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.
Show that the number $a=3(3-2i)+2(5+3i)$ is real.
Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=4x-1$. Compute $f(1)+f(2)+\ldots+f(10)$.
Solve the equation $\log_2(2x)=\log_2(1+x)$ in the set of real numbers.
After a price increase of $10\%$, the price of a product is $2200$ lei. Compute the price of the product before the increase.
Determine the real number $a$ for which the vectors $\vec{u}=\vec{i}+4\vec{j}$ and $\vec{v}=2\vec{i}+(a+1)\vec{j}$ are collinear.
Determine $x\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, knowing that $\dfrac{3\sin x+\cos x}{\sin x}=4$.

Consider the determinant $D(a,b)=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\a&a^2&1\\b&b^2&1\end{vmatrix}$, where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers.

(a) Show that $D(2,3)=2$.

(b) Check whether $D(a,b)=(a-1)(b-1)(b-a)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

(c) In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $P_n(n,n^2)$, where $n$ is a nonzero natural number. Determine the natural number $n$, $n\ge3$, for which the area of triangle $P_1P_2P_n$ is equal to $1$.

Let $x_1,x_2,x_3$ be the complex roots of the polynomial $f=X^3-4X^2+3X-m$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) For $m=4$, show that $f(4)=8$.

(b) Determine the real number $m$ for which the roots of the polynomial $f$ satisfy the relation $x_1+x_2=x_3$.

(c) If $x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3=7(x_1+x_2+x_3)$, show that $f$ is divisible by $X-3$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\cos x+\dfrac{x^2}{2}$.

(a) Compute $f'(x)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the equation of the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of the graph with abscissa $x_0=0$.

(c) Prove that $f(x)\ge1$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

For every nonzero natural number $n$ consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 x^ne^x\,dx$.

(a) Compute $I_1$.

(b) Show that $I_{n+1}+(n+1)I_n=e$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.

(c) Show that $1\le(n+1)I_n\le e$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.
Determine the common ratio of the geometric progression $(b_n)_{n\ge1}$ with real terms, knowing that $b_1=1$ and $b_4=27$.
Determine the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola associated with the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-6x+8$.
Solve the equation $3^{x+2}=9^{1-x}$ in the set of real numbers.
Compute the probability that, choosing at random a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, it is a perfect square.
Consider the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ such that $\overrightarrow{AB}=4\vec{i}-3\vec{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=2\vec{i}-5\vec{j}$. Determine the length of the vector $\overrightarrow{AC}$.
Compute the sine of the angle $A$ of the triangle $ABC$ in which $AB=4$, $BC=5$ and $\sin C=\dfrac{4}{5}$.

For every real number $m$ consider the matrix $A(m)=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\m&0&0\\m&0&m\end{pmatrix}$.

(a) Compute $\det\left(A(1)\right)$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $m$ knowing that $A(m)\cdot A(-m)=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&0\\1&1&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$.

(c) Show that $\det\left(A(1)+A(2)+\ldots+A(101)\right)=-51^2\cdot101^3$.

On the set of real numbers the associative law of composition $x\circ y=xy-4x-4y+20$ is defined.

(a) Compute $3\circ4$.

(b) Show that $x\circ y=(x-4)(y-4)+4$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

(c) Solve the equation $\underbrace{x\circ x\circ\ldots\circ x}_{x\text{ appears }2013\text{ times}}=5$ in the set of real numbers.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{e^x}{x+e^x}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{(x-1)e^x}{\left(x+e^x\right)^2}$ for every $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the equation of the asymptote to the graph of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.

(c) Prove that $f(x)\ge\dfrac{e}{e+1}$ for every $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

For every natural number $n$ consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 xe^{-nx^2}\,dx$.

(a) Compute $I_0$.

(b) Show that $I_{n+1}\le I_n$ for every natural number $n$.

(c) Prove that $I_n=\dfrac{1}{2n}\left(1-\dfrac{1}{e^n}\right)$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.
Determine the real number $x$ for which the numbers $1$, $2x+2$ and $7$ are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression.
Compute the distance between the points of intersection with the axis $Ox$ of the graph of the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-4x+3$.
Solve the equation $\sqrt{x^2+4}=x+2$ in the set of real numbers.
Determine how many odd natural numbers $\overline{ab}$ can be formed, knowing that $a,b\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ and $a\ne b$.

In the rectangle $ABCD$, with $AB=8$ and $BC=6$, consider the vector $\vec{v}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{AO}+\overrightarrow{AD}$, where $\{O\}=AC\cap BD$. Compute the length of the vector $\vec{v}$.
Compute the sine of the angle $A$ of the triangle $ABC$ in which $AB=6$, $BC=10$ and $\sin C=\dfrac{3}{5}$.

For every real number $a$ consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a&1&1\\1&a&1\\1&1&a\end{pmatrix}$.

(a) Compute $\det\left(A(0)\right)$.

(b) Determine the real values of $a$ for which $5A(a)-\left(A(a)\right)^2=4I_3$.

(c) Determine the inverse of the matrix $A(2)$.

Consider the polynomial $f=X^3-mX^2+3X-1$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) Compute $f(2)-f(-2)$.

(b) Determine the remainder of the division of $f$ by $X+2$, knowing that the remainder of the division of the polynomial $f$ by $X-2$ is equal to $9$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $m$ for which $x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3=3$, where $x_1,x_2,x_3$ are the roots of the polynomial $f$.

Consider the function $f:(-1,1)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\ln\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}$.

(a) Compute $f'(x)$, $x\in(-1,1)$.

(b) Check whether the function $f$ is decreasing on the interval $(-1,1)$.

(c) Determine the inflection points of the function $f$.

For every natural number $n$ consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_1^2 x^ne^x\,dx$.

(a) Compute $I_0$.

(b) Show that $I_1=e^2$.

(c) Prove that $I_{n+1}+(n+1)I_n=2^{n+1}e^2-e$ for every natural number $n$.
Compute the sum of the first three terms of the arithmetic progression $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$, knowing that $a_1=6$ and $a_2=12$.
Determine the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola associated with the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+2x+4$.
Solve the equation $(3^x-1)(3^x-3)=0$ in the set of real numbers.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, it contains the digit $1$.
Consider the equilateral triangle $ABC$ with $AB=2$. Compute the length of the vector $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}$.
Compute the area of the isosceles triangle $ABC$, knowing that $A=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $AC=4$.

Consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}2&a&a\\a&2&2\\a&a&2\end{pmatrix}$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det\left(A(0)\right)=8$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $a$ for which $\det\left(A(a)\right)=0$.

(c) Determine the matrix $X=\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$, knowing that $A(1)\cdot X=\begin{pmatrix}4\\5\\4\end{pmatrix}$.

Let $x_1,x_2,x_3$ be the roots of the polynomial $f=X^3-2X^2+3X+m$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) Compute $f(1)$.

(b) Show that $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=-2$.

(c) Determine the real number $m$, knowing that $x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3=8$.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln x}{x}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}$, $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the equation of the asymptote to the graph of the function $f$ at $+\infty$.

(c) Show that $f(x)\le\dfrac{1}{e}$ for every $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+x+1$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=\frac{11}{6}$.

(b) For every nonzero natural number $n$ consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1\frac{x^n}{f(x)}\,dx$. Show that $I_{n+1}\le I_n$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.

(c) Determine the positive real number $a$, knowing that $\displaystyle\int_0^a\frac{2x+1}{f(x)}\,dx=\ln3$.
Determine the real part of the complex number $z=1+2i+3i^2$.
Determine the coordinates of the intersection point of the graphs of the functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x-1$ and $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=3x-5$.
Solve the equation $3^{x^2-x}=3^{2x}$ in the set of real numbers.
Determine how many even two-digit natural numbers can be formed with the digits $0$, $1$, $2$ and $3$.

In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}=3\vec{i}+2\vec{j}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=(m+1)\vec{i}+4\vec{j}$, where $m$ is a real number. Determine the real number $m$, knowing that $\overrightarrow{AC}=2\overrightarrow{AB}$.
Consider the triangle $ABC$ with $AB=AC=3$ and $BC=3\sqrt{2}$. Determine $\cos C$.

Consider the matrix $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\x&1&0\\2x^2-2x&4x&1\end{pmatrix}$, where $x$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det\left(A(0)\right)=1$.

Consider the matrix $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2^x&4^x\\1&x&2x\end{pmatrix}$, where $x$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det\left(A(1)\right)=1$.

(b) Prove that $\det\left(A(x)\right)=\left(2^x-1\right)\left(2^x+x-x\cdot2^x\right)$ for every real number $x$.

(c) Show that $A(1)+A(2)+A(3)+\ldots+A(2017)=\begin{pmatrix}2017&2017&2017\\2017&2\left(2^{2017}-1\right)&\frac{4}{3}\left(4^{2017}-1\right)\\2017&2017\cdot1009&2017\cdot2018\end{pmatrix}$.

On the set of real numbers the associative law of composition $x*y=7xy+7x+7y+6$ is defined.

(a) Show that $x*y=7(x+1)(y+1)-1$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $x$ for which $x*x*x=x$.

(c) Prove that if $a$, $b$ and $c$ are natural numbers such that $a*b*c=48$, then the numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ are equal.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-3}{e^x}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{-x^2+2x+3}{e^x}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the equation of the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of the graph with abscissa $x=-1$.

(c) Prove that $-2e\le f(x)\le\dfrac{6}{e^3}$ for every $x\in[-1,+\infty)$.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{(x+1)^2}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_1^2\frac{x+1}{\sqrt{x}}f(x)\,dx=\ln\frac{3}{2}$.

(b) Prove that every antiderivative of the function $f$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(0,+\infty)$.

(c) Determine the real number $m$, $m>0$, knowing that the plane region bounded by the graph of the function $g:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\sqrt{x}(x+1)f(x)$, the axis $Ox$ and the lines with equations $x=1$ and $x=2$ has area equal to $1-\ln\dfrac{m+1}{m}$.
Determine the complex number $z$, given that $2\overline{z}-z=1-3i$, where $\overline{z}$ is the conjugate of $z$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-mx+1$, where $m$ is a real number. Determine the real numbers $m$, given that the vertex of the parabola associated with the function $f$ lies on the axis $Ox$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $\dfrac{\lg x}{\lg(x+2)}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, it has distinct and odd digits.

In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the point $A(-5,2)$ and the line $d$ with equation $y=x+1$. Determine the equation of the line that passes through the point $A$ and is perpendicular to the line $d$.
Show that $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+x\right)-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-x\right)=0$ for every real number $x$.

Consider the matrix $M(m)=\begin{pmatrix}2m&1&1\\1&2m&1\\1&1&2m\end{pmatrix}$ and the system of equations $\begin{cases}2mx+y+z=-1\\x+2my+z=0\\x+y+2mz=1\end{cases}$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(M(0))=2$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $m$ such that $\det(M(m))=0$.

(c) For $m=-1$, prove that if $(a,b,c)$ is a solution of the system, then at most one of the numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ is an integer.

On the set of real numbers the associative law of composition $x*y=4xy+3x+3y+\dfrac{3}{2}$ is defined.

(a) Prove that $x*y=4\left(x+\dfrac{3}{4}\right)\left(y+\dfrac{3}{4}\right)-\dfrac{3}{4}$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

(b) Determine the real number $x$ for which $x*x*x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $a$ such that $f(x)*f(y)=f(x+y)$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, where $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=ae^x-\dfrac{3}{4}$.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=8x^2-\ln x$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{(4x-1)(4x+1)}{x}$, $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(b) Prove that the point $A\left(\dfrac{2}{3},3\right)$ lies on the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of abscissa $x=1$ on the graph of $f$.

(c) Prove that $f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)<f\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\right)<f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

Consider the function $f:(-3,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+3}{x+3}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 (x+3)f(x)\,dx=4$.

(b) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=2-3\ln\dfrac{4}{3}$.

(c) For every natural number $n$, consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 e^x(x+3)^n\left(f(x)\right)^n dx$. Prove that $I_n+2nI_{n-1}=e\cdot 5^n-3^n$ for every natural number $n$, $n\ge 1$.
Show that the number $n=\left|1-\sqrt{2}\right|+\left|2-\sqrt{2}\right|$ is a natural number.
Consider the functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=11-x$ and $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=1-11x$. Solve in the set of real numbers the inequality $f(x)\ge g(x)$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $3^x\cdot 2^{x+1}=72$.
Determine how many three-digit natural numbers with distinct digits can be formed using only odd digits.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(-3,3)$, $B(1,3)$ and $C(1,5)$. Compute the area of the triangle $ABC$.
Compute the length of the radius of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, given that $BC=4$, $B=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $C=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Consider the matrix $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&x-2&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&e^{x-2}\end{pmatrix}$, where $x$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(A(2))=1$.

(b) Prove that $A(x)A(y)=A(x+y-2)$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $m$ for which $A(1)A(2)A(3)\cdot\ldots\cdot A(10)=A\left(m^2+m+17\right)$.

Consider the polynomial $f=X^3-4X^2+5X+a$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $f(1)-f(-1)=12$.

(b) Determine the real number $a$, given that the polynomial $f$ is divisible by the polynomial $X-2$.

(c) Determine the real number $a$, given that all the roots of the polynomial $f$ are integers.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\ln x$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{2-\ln x}{2x\sqrt{x}}$, $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the abscissa of the point on the graph of the function $f$ at which the tangent to the graph of $f$ is perpendicular to the axis $Oy$.

(c) Prove that $2^{\sqrt{3}}<3^{\sqrt{2}}$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=4x-x^2$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx=9$.

(b) Show that $\displaystyle\int_1^2\dfrac{2-x}{f(x)}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\dfrac{4}{3}$.

(c) For every nonzero natural number $n$, consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^4 f^n(x)\,dx$. Prove that $I_{n+1}\le 4I_n$ for every nonzero natural number $n$.
Consider the complex number $z=1-2i$. Show that $z^2-2z+5=0$.
Determine the real numbers $a$ and $b$ for which the graphs of the functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=2x+a$ and $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=bx+2$ intersect at the point $M(2,8)$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $\log_3(4x+5)=1+\log_3(x+3)$.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, it has even digits.

In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(2,2)$, $B(4,1)$ and $C(0,8)$. Determine the length of the segment $CM$, given that $M$ is the reflection of the point $A$ in the point $B$.
Compute the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$, given that $AB=6$, $AC=10$ and $m(\angle BAC)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Consider the matrix $M(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\a+1&-1&1\\1&1&-a\end{pmatrix}$ and the system of equations $\begin{cases}x+y+z=2\\(a+1)x-y+z=0\\x+y-az=1\end{cases}$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(M(-1))=0$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $a$ for which $\det(M(a))=0$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $a$ such that the system has a unique solution $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ and $2x_0+y_0z_0=0$.

On the set of real numbers the associative law of composition $x*y=\dfrac{1}{10}xy-(x+y)+20$ is defined.

(a) Prove that $x*y=\dfrac{1}{10}(x-10)(y-10)+10$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

(b) Determine the real values of $x$ for which $x*x\le\dfrac{101}{10}$.

(c) Compute $\log_2 1*\log_2 2*\log_2 3*\ldots*\log_2 2018$.

Consider the function $f:(-1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=2x^3-3x^2+6x-6\ln(x+1)$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{6x^3}{x+1}$, $x\in(-1,+\infty)$.

(b) Prove that the minimum value of the function $f$ is $0$.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{f(x)}}{x}$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\left(x^2+x+1\right)e^x$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)e^{-x}\,dx=\dfrac{11}{6}$.

(b) Prove that every antiderivative of the function $f$ has exactly two inflection points.

(c) Show that $\lim\limits_{t\to 0}\dfrac{1}{t}\displaystyle\int_0^t f(x)\,dx=1$.
Show that the number $n=\left(3-i\sqrt{2}\right)\left(3+i\sqrt{2}\right)$ is an integer, where $i^2=-1$.
Determine the real number $a$, given that the point $A(a,3)$ lies on the graph of the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=2x+a$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $2019^x+2019^{-x}=2$.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, its units digit is odd.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(3,-3)$ and $B(2,-2)$. Determine the equation of the line $d$ that passes through $A$ and is perpendicular to $AB$.
Show that $\sin(a-b)\sin(a+b)=(\sin a-\sin b)(\sin a+\sin b)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

Consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a&0&-a\\0&2&0\\-a&0&a\end{pmatrix}$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(A(a))=0$ for every real number $a$.

(b) Prove that $A(a)A(b)=2A(ab)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

(c) Prove that all the entries of the matrix $B=A(\log_2 3)\cdot A(\log_3 4)\cdot A(\log_4 5)\cdot\ldots\cdot A(\log_{15}16)$ are integers.

Consider the polynomial $f=X^3+X^2+mX+n$, where $m$ and $n$ are real numbers.

(a) Show that $f(-1)-2f(0)+f(1)=2$ for all real numbers $m$ and $n$.

(b) Determine the real numbers $m$ and $n$, given that the polynomial $f$ is divisible by the polynomial $X^2-1$.

(c) Prove that $3\left(x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3+x_1x_2x_3\right)-\left(x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3\right)=1$ for all real numbers $m$ and $n$, where $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ are the roots of the polynomial $f$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2e^{-x}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=x(2-x)e^{-x}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the intervals of monotonicity of the function $f$.

(c) Prove that, for every $a\in\left(0,4e^{-2}\right)$, the equation $f(x)=a$ has exactly three real solutions.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+\ln x$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_1^2\left(f(x)-\ln x\right)dx=\dfrac{7}{3}$.

(b) Prove that the plane region bounded by the graph of the function $g:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=2x-x^2+f(x)$, the axis $Ox$ and the lines with equations $x=1$ and $x=e$ has area equal to $e^2$.

(c) Prove that $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty}\displaystyle\int_{e^{-1}}^1 x^n\left(f(x)-x^2\right)dx=0$.
Show that the sum of the elements of the set $A=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\mid n-1\le 4\}$ is equal to $15$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2-2x+m$, where $m$ is a real number. Determine the real number $m$, given that the vertex of the parabola associated with the function $f$ has ordinate equal to $2$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $\sqrt{x+3}=\sqrt{9-x}$.
Determine the number of subsets with at least $8$ elements of a set with exactly $10$ elements.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(5,1)$, $B(-1,3)$ and $C(8,10)$. Determine the length of the segment $CD$, where the point $D$ is the midpoint of the segment $AB$.
Show that $1+\cos\pi+\cos 2\pi+\cos 3\pi+\ldots+\cos 2019\pi=0$.

Consider the matrices $I_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a+1&0&0\\1&a&1\\0&0&a+1\end{pmatrix}$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(A(1))=4$.

(b) Prove that $A(a)A(b)=abI_3+(a+b+1)A(0)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

(c) Determine the natural number $n$ for which $A(0)A(1)A(2)\ldots A(2019)=n!\,A(0)$.

Consider the polynomial $f=X^3-mX^2+2X+3-m$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) Determine the real number $m$, given that $f(1)=0$.

(b) For $m=3$, determine the roots of the polynomial $f$.

(c) Determine the real number $m$ for which $x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3=\left(x_1+x_2+x_3\right)^3-12$, where $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ are the roots of the polynomial $f$.

Consider the function $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=1-\dfrac{2}{x+1}-\ln\dfrac{x}{x+1}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{x(x+1)^2}$, $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the equation of the horizontal asymptote at $+\infty$ to the graph of the function $f$.

(c) Consider the functions $g:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$ and $h:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $h(x)=\ln\dfrac{x}{x+1}$. Prove that the graphs of the functions $g$ and $h$ have no common point.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2+4}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f^2(x)\,dx=\dfrac{13}{3}$.

(b) Show that the plane region bounded by the graph of the function $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=xf(x)$, the axis $Ox$ and the lines with equations $x=-1$ and $x=1$ has area equal to $\dfrac{10\sqrt{5}-16}{3}$.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{1}{x^4}\displaystyle\int_0^x t^3f(t)\,dt$.
Consider the complex numbers $z_1=3-i$ and $z_2=8-3i$. Show that $3z_1-z_2=1$.
Determine the real number $a$ for which $f(a)+f(a+1)=35$, where $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x-5$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $2\cdot 4^x-4^{x+1}+32=0$.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number $n$ from the set of one-digit natural numbers, it satisfies the relation $n(n+1)\ge 42$.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(8,4)$, $B(0,6)$ and $C(m,5)$. Determine the real number $m$, given that $\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{CB}$.
Compute the length of the hypotenuse $BC$ of the right triangle $ABC$, given that $AB=6$ and the area of the triangle $ABC$ is equal to $24$.

Consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a+1&0&0\\0&1&\ln(a+1)\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, where $a$ is a real number, $a>0$.

(a) Show that $\det(A(1))=2$.

(b) Prove that $A(a)A(b)=A(ab+a+b)$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$, $a>0$, $b>0$.

(c) Determine the real number $a$, $a>0$, given that $A(a)A(a)A(a)=A(7)$.

Let $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ be the roots of the polynomial $f=X^3+mX^2-mX+2$, where $m$ is a real number.

(a) Determine the real number $m$, given that $f(-2)=0$.

(b) For $m=1$, determine the roots of the polynomial $f$.

(c) Consider $a=\dfrac{x_1^2+mx_1}{x_2x_3}+\dfrac{x_2^2+mx_2}{x_1x_3}+\dfrac{x_3^2+mx_3}{x_1x_2}$. Prove that $a\in[3,+\infty)$ for every real number $m$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=e^x\left(x^2+4x+1\right)$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=e^x(x+5)(x+1)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the abscissas of the points on the graph of the function $f$ at which the tangent to the graph of $f$ is parallel to the axis $Ox$.

(c) Determine the real values of $a$ for which the equation $f(x)=a$ has exactly three real solutions.

Consider the function $f:(1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\ln x}$.

(a) Show that every antiderivative of the function $f$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(1,+\infty)$.

(b) Compute $\displaystyle\int_e^{e^2}\dfrac{1}{x}f(x)\,dx$.

(c) Determine the real number $a$, $a>e$, given that the plane region bounded by the graph of the function $g:(1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$, the axis $Ox$ and the lines with equations $x=e$ and $x=a$ has area equal to $2a$.
Show that the number $z=\left(1-i\sqrt{2}\right)\left(1+i\sqrt{2}\right)$ is a natural number, where $i^2=-1$.
Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=3x+a$, where $a$ is a real number. Determine the real number $a$, given that $f(x)+f(1-x)=7$ for every real number $x$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $5^x+5^{-x}=2$.
Consider the set $A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. Determine the number of three-element subsets of $A$ that contain $1$.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the point $M(-4,4)$. Determine the equation of the line $d$ that passes through the point $M$ and is perpendicular to the line $OM$.
The triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $A$ and $\sin B=\cos B$. Show that the triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

Consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a&a+1&a+2\\a^2+1&a^2+2&a^2+3\\1&2&4\end{pmatrix}$, where $a$ is a real number.

(a) Show that $\det(A(0))=-1$.

(b) Prove that, for every real number $a$, the matrix $A(a)$ is invertible.

(c) Determine the integers $a$ for which the inverse of the matrix $A(a)$ has all its entries integers.

On the set $A=[1,+\infty)$ the law of composition $x*y=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt[3]{x^3y^3-x^3-y^3+9}$ is defined.

(a) Show that $1*2020=1$.

(b) Prove that $x*y=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{1}{8}\left(x^3-1\right)\left(y^3-1\right)+1}$ for all $x,y\in A$.

(c) Determine $x\in A$ for which $x*x=x$.

Consider the function $f:(2,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x-2}+\ln\dfrac{x-1}{x}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{-3x+4}{x(x-1)(x-2)^2}$, $x\in(2,+\infty)$.

(b) Determine the equation of the horizontal asymptote at $+\infty$ to the graph of the function $f$.

(c) Prove that $\dfrac{1}{x-2}>\ln\dfrac{x}{x-1}$ for every $x\in(2,+\infty)$.

Consider the function $f:(-1,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^3+1}}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(x^3+1\right)f^2(x)\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

(b) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f^2(x)\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3}\ln 2$.

(c) For every nonzero natural number $n$, consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 f\left(x^n\right)dx$. Prove that $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty}I_n=0$.
Consider the complex number $z=2+i$. Show that $z^2-4z+5=0$.
Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+x+a$, where $a$ is a real number. Determine the real number $a$, given that the point $M(0,2)$ lies on the graph of the function $f$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $x=\sqrt[3]{x^3+2x}$.

Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of five-digit natural numbers with distinct digits formed with digits from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, it has the tens digit equal to $2$ and the units digit equal to $3$.

In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $A(0,1)$, $B(2,3)$ and $C(4,a)$, where $a$ is a real number. Determine the real number $a$, given that the point $C$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment $AB$.

The measures of the angles $A$, $B$ and $C$ of the triangle $ABC$ are, in this order, consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression. Prove that the measure of the angle $B$ is equal to $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Consider the matrix $A(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1+\ln x\\0&x&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$, where $x\in(0,+\infty)$.

(a) Show that $\det(A(1))=1$.

(b) Prove that $A(x)A(y)=A(y)A(x)$ for all $x,y\in(0,+\infty)$.

On the set of real numbers the law of composition $x*y=xy-4(x+y)+a$ is defined, where $a$ is a real number.

(b) For $a=20$, show that $e=5$ is the identity element of the law of composition "$*$".

(c) Prove that, if $a\in[20,+\infty)$, then the set $H=[4,+\infty)$ is a stable subset of the set of real numbers with respect to the law of composition "$*$".

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to(0,+\infty)$, $f(x)=6^x-3^x+2^x$.

(a) Show that $f'(0)=\ln 4$.

(b) Consider the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of abscissa $x=0$ on the graph of $f$. Determine the real number $a$ for which the point $A\left(a,\ln(16e)\right)$ lies on this tangent.

(c) Compute $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\ln\left(f(x)\right)}{x}$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=1-\dfrac{2x}{x^2+3}-\dfrac{2}{x^2+3}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_1^2\left(x^2+3\right)f(x)\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

(b) Show that $\displaystyle\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx=1-\ln\dfrac{4}{3}-\dfrac{\pi\sqrt{3}}{9}$.

(c) For every nonzero natural number $n$, consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_0^1 f^n(x)\,dx$. Show that $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty}I_n=0$.
Show that the number $a=3+2\sqrt{2}+\dfrac{1}{3+2\sqrt{2}}$ is a natural number.
Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=2x+1$. Show that $(f\circ f)(1)=f(2)+2$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $9^{x^2}=3\cdot 3^x$.
Determine the nonzero natural number $n$, given that the set $A=\{1,2,3,\ldots,n\}$ has exactly $10$ two-element subsets.
In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $M(1,0)$, $N(7,0)$ and $A(a,3)$, where $a$ is a real number. Given that $AM=AN$, show that the segment $AO$ has length equal to $5$.

Consider the matrix $A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&2-a&a\\a&1&1\\a&2a-5&a-2\end{pmatrix}$ and the system of equations $\begin{cases}x+(2-a)y+az=1\\ax+y+z=2-a\\ax+(2a-5)y+(a-2)z=-4\end{cases}$, where $a$ is a real number.

On the set of real numbers the law of composition $x*y=\log_2\left(2^x+2^y\right)$ is defined.

(a) Show that $0*0=1$.

(b) Prove that the law of composition "$*$" is commutative.

(c) Determine the real number $x$ for which $(x*x)*x=3+\log_2 3$.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\sqrt{x^4-x^2+1}$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{x\left(2x^2-1\right)}{\sqrt{x^4-x^2+1}}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the equation of the tangent to the graph of the function $f$ at the point of abscissa $x=1$ on the graph of $f$.

(c) Prove that, for every $m\in\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},1\right)$, the equation $f(x)=m$ has exactly four real solutions.

Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{x^2+2x+5}$.

(a) Show that $\displaystyle\int_1^2 x\cdot\dfrac{1}{f(x)}\,dx=\dfrac{31}{3}$.

(c) For every nonzero natural number $n$, consider the number $I_n=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1 x^{2n-1}f(x)\,dx$. Prove that $\lim\limits_{n\to+\infty}I_n=0$.
Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^2+ax-5$, where $a$ is a real number. Determine the real number $a$, given that the point $M(1,2)$ lies on the graph of the function $f$.
Solve in the set of real numbers the equation $\log_4\left(x^2+1\right)=\log_4 x+\log_4(x+1)$.
Compute the probability that, choosing a number from the set of two-digit natural numbers, it is divisible by $2$ and by $5$.

In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$ consider the points $M(3,4)$, $N(0,1)$ and $P(3,0)$. Determine the equation of the line $d$ that passes through the point $P$ and is parallel to the line $MN$.
Consider the triangle $ABC$, right-angled at $C$. Show that $\tan B=\dfrac{1}{\tan A}$.

(a) Show that $\det(A(0))=8$.

(b) Determine the matrix $B\in M_3(\mathbb{R})$, given that $aB=A(a)-2I_3$ for every real number $a$.

(a) Show that $2*0=2$.

(b) Prove that, if $a$ and $b$ are real numbers such that $a\le b$, then $a*b=b$.

(c) Determine the real numbers $x$ for which $(2x)*\left(x^2+1\right)*(-2x)=10$.

(a) Show that $f'(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+3}-x}{\sqrt{x^2+3}}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Determine the equation of the horizontal asymptote at $+\infty$ to the graph of the function $f$.

(c) Determine the set of real values of $a$ for which the equation $f(x)=a$ has a solution.
